one_month_reasoning: One major scheduled event falls in the window: Q3 2026 results on Oct 28, 2026 (call at 1 PM ET), two trading days before the Oct 30 close (Oct 31 is a Saturday). The guide is $9.3-9.4B in sales and $0.70-0.71 post-split adjusted EPS. Amphenol beat the top of its guide by a wide margin in each of the last two quarters: Q1 adj EPS $1.06 pre-split (Q4-25 guide not re-checked), and Q2 $1.35 against a $1.14-1.16 guide, or about $1.31 without tariff recoveries. Q2 orders were $10.7B (book-to-bill 1.23), and at Citi on Sept 9 management called demand 'robust and not short-term'. So I expect a beat (roughly $0.76-0.80) and a Q4 guide above consensus. But the stock sits about 4% below its 52-week high at about 26x 2027 consensus EPS, so a beat is largely expected, and the reaction risks are an uneven AI ramp in the Q4 guide and a mid-teens sequential decline in communications networks. I tilt the centre up only slightly (median about $86.6, +1%), with a log-sd of 0.135. That is somewhat wider than the 46%/3.5 = 13% rule of thumb, to allow for the earnings gap.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%): 2028E EPS $3.78 x 25x = $94.5, and FCF yield (40%): 2028E FCF $8.0B / 3.5% = $229B equity / 2.578B diluted post-split shares = $88.7. Both are values as of Oct 2027 on next-year numbers.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2028E adj EPS $3.78 (2027 consensus $3.29 x 1.15) x 25x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus implies 2027 growth of +23% (3.29/2.67). I assume deceleration to 15% in 2028 once the CommScope accretion has lapped, as AI datacom (43% of Q2 sales, +63% organic) normalises. Book-to-bill of 1.23 and management's 'robust, not short-term' demand comment argue against a sharper slowdown.

Today's price of $85.67 divided by 2027 consensus EPS of $3.29 gives 26.0x. I take one turn of derating as growth slows from about 50% in 2026 to mid-teens. The 29.8% adjusted operating margin and 1.3x net leverage support a premium multiple.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2028E FCF $8.0B at a 3.5% equity FCF yield; 2.578B diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 2026 weighted diluted shares of 1,289.2M x 2 for the 2-for-1 split distributed Sept 2, 2026.

2028E EPS of $3.78 x 2.578B shares gives about $9.7B of adjusted net income. I apply about 82% FCF conversion: H1-26 ran at 65% because of a $1.18B working-capital build, while the long-run average is roughly 85% or more. Capex runs at the high end of 3-4% of sales, per the Q2 call.
Current market cap is about $221B ($85.67 x 2.578B). Against my 2027E FCF of about $6.8B ($3.29 x 2.578B x 80%), that is a 3.1% yield. I widen it to 3.5% for slower growth by late 2027.
Total debt of $18.8B less $5.4B of cash and short-term investments at June 30, 2026. It is already reflected in the equity FCF after interest.

bear.story: AI/datacom orders digest in 2027 (hyperscaler capex pause or a delayed customer ramp). Book-to-bill falls below 1 and 2028E EPS slips to about $3.2. The multiple derates to about 18x, a cyclical-connector level, giving about $58.

base.story: Beats continue but growth decelerates to mid-teens in 2028. Margins hold near 29-30% and CommScope delivers. EPS of about $3.78 at about 25x gives $93-95.

bull.story: The AI interconnect content ramp (copper, optics and power) runs ahead of consensus, as in 2026 when quarters beat the top of the guide by 15%+. 2028E EPS reaches about $4.4 at 28x, giving about $123.

thesis_break_reason: $60 is about 30% below today, back at the 52-week low ($59.01) and about 18x 2027 consensus EPS. Ordinary 46%-vol noise rarely reaches that within a year without fundamental news. Trading there would most likely mean AI datacom orders, now 43% of sales and the source of most growth, have rolled over: book-to-bill below 1, or a guide below consensus. Other possible causes are margin damage from integration or a large adverse tax or tariff outcome (the China tax matter has already produced $230M in payment notices).

Q4 2026 results and Q1 2027 guide; first full-year read of CommScope (~$4.6B sales target)

key_uncertainties: Durability of AI datacom demand (43% of sales, +63% organic in Q2-26), and whether 2027 brings digestion
How much of the 2026 margin step-up (29.8% adj OPM, including $80M of tariff recoveries) is structural
Multiple sustainability: today about 26x 2027 consensus for a company whose growth is likely to halve
Optics architecture shifts (co-packaged optics) changing interconnect content, partly hedged by CommScope's optical exposure (>75% optics)
Tax rate creep (adjusted ETR raised to 27%) and the China tax dispute
M&A: large deals add upside but also execution and leverage risk
reasoning: Everything is post-split (2-for-1 distributed Sept 2, 2026), so pre-split filing figures are halved. Primary documents show exceptional momentum. Q2-26 sales were $8.76B (+55%, +30% organic) with adj EPS of $1.35 pre-split against a $1.14-1.16 guide. Orders were $10.7B (book-to-bill 1.23) and the adjusted operating margin was 29.8%. The Q3 guide is $9.3-9.4B in sales and $0.70-0.71 post-split EPS. CommScope was raised to $4.6B in sales and $0.30 of accretion. Net debt is $13.4B (1.3x). Details the recaps skip: the 10-Q shows a $1.18B H1 working-capital build that held FCF conversion to about 65%; the adjusted tax rate rose to 27% after $230M in China tax notices; and the CEO and a director exercised and sold expiring options in late July and August. Those sales look routine (low-strike options), so I treat them as neutral. At Citi (Sept 9) management called demand robust while admitting AI customer ramps are uneven ('one foot on the gas and one on the brake'). Valuation comes out at about $92 (P/E $94.5 and FCF yield $88.7), about 8% above spot. Consensus 2027 EPS is $3.29, and the split-adjusted analyst average target of $99 is used only as a cross-check. Scenarios are bear $58 (25%), base $93 (50%) and bull $123 (25%). For the ladder I used a mixture: 80% lognormal centred at $93 with sd 0.33, and 20% bear lognormal centred at $65 with sd 0.40. That gives a median of about $87.5, P(>=86) = 52%, and a fat left tail reflecting AI-cycle concentration risk. The overall dispersion is consistent with the 46% realised vol, slightly trimmed on the upside because the starting multiple is high. Twelve Data fundamentals and estimates were paywalled, so consensus came from one web aggregator.
